title: Data-Efficient Learning of High-Quality Controls for Kinodynamic Planning used in Vehicular Navigation
venue: Machine Learning for Motion Planning (MLMP) Workshop at ICRA 2021
extended_summary:
This paper addresses the problem of improving the practical performance of kinodynamic motion planning for vehicular robotic systems. The authors focus on the difficulty of obtaining high-quality trajectories when planners rely on random controls for expansion, which often leads to slow convergence and higher-cost paths.

They propose a supervised learning framework that learns a controller offline. The model takes a difference vector between the current state and a local goal state as input and returns a control and propagation duration that should move the system closer to that local target. The training data are generated efficiently using discretization, propagation, pruning, and additional random sampling to ensure target dispersion and retain only higher-quality controls. The paper also introduces two planner-side waypoint-generation strategies: an exploratory sample-based expansion and an exploitative medial-axis-based expansion.

The approach is evaluated in simulation on first-order and second-order differential drive systems in city benchmark environments derived from real-world maps, including Berlin, London, and Boston. The learned controller is integrated into the DIRT kinodynamic planner and compared against random-control baselines and blossom-expansion variants. The paper reports that the learned-controller methods produce lower-cost paths in fewer iterations and less time than traditional random propagation, and that medial-axis expansion further improves path quality and convergence speed.
quality_tier_rationale: This is a robotics motion-planning paper, not an education study, and it does not evaluate any K-12 teaching or learning intervention. No education-relevant empirical design is present for the requested taxonomy.
impact_tier_rationale: The paper reports performance improvements for vehicular navigation planning, with no demonstrated impact on K-12 educational outcomes, teacher planning, or instructional coaching.
